author: Preston Stober
title: Hartford church not letting priest to return after police close investigation into alleged theft of funds - NewsBreak
text: HARTFORD, Conn. (WTNH) — Earlier this year, Father Charles Jacobs of Holy Trinity Church in Hartford was accused of taking church funds for personal use . A Hartford Police Department investigation was opened and he was put on administrative leave where he remains to this day. But this week, parishioners at Holy Trinity Church received a blast email saying Father Jacobs is officially in the clear as far as the law goes. The Hartford police confirmed with News 8 that they have closed their investigation due to insufficient evidence. Father Jacobs has been away from the church since February and without a full-time priest, the church is down to one service a week. But The Archdiocese of Hartford said Father Jacobs is still not welcome back as they have an open investigation of their own. The archdiocese sent News 8 a statement, saying in part, “Father Jacobs is still facing a canonical process. He has retained a canon lawyer and the church process will continue. In the meantime, Father Jacobs remains on administrative leave and will continue to receive salary and benefits as he has throughout his suspension.” In late June, the church said that Father Jacobs will not be returning, period. Father Jacobs himself does not deny taking church funds. He told News 8’s Dennis House in an exclusive interview that he never used funds for personal purposes. “People would need gas, they would need food, they would need medication. I would use those parish funds to give to those people that would come to me in need,” Father Jacobs said earlier this year. “Each week I would put aside maybe $80 or so of that money so that I would have it over the course of the week to give to people when they came to me.” The church told News 8 that Father Jacobs was lying in the interview.
